title: Dark Chocolate and Orange Liqueur Truffle Cookies
story: Orange and dark chocolate have been working together long enough that nobody questions it anymore. What makes these different is that the liqueur goes into the dough, not a ganache — the citrus infuses the whole thing rather than sitting on top. Roll them in cocoa before they go in the oven, dust them with powdered sugar when they come out. They look like something from a bakery case. They're easier than that.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
¼ cup orange liqueur (Grand Marnier or Cointreau)
¼ cup cocoa powder, for rolling

steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, ½ tsp baking powder, and ¼ tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter, ¼ cup granulated sugar, and ½ cup packed brown sugar together until light and creamy, about 2–3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look pale and fluffy, not dense or grainy.

steps.text: Beat in 2 large eggs one at a time, fully incorporating each before adding the next.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract and ¼ cup orange liqueur.
Fold in ½ cup dark chocolate chips.
Add the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain.
Cover the dough and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The dough will be too soft to roll before chilling — don't skip this.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Spread ¼ cup cocoa powder in a shallow bowl.
Roll the chilled dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each one in cocoa powder until fully coated. Place 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.

steps.donenessCue: Edges should look set and firm while centers still look slightly soft and underdone — these are fudgy cookies, not cakey ones. The cocoa coating makes the edges hard to read; press the edge of one gently with a finger, it should feel just firm.

steps.text: Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
Once fully cooled, dust generously with powdered sugar just before serving. Don't dust too early — the sugar will absorb into the cookies as they sit.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Chill the dough overnight instead of 1 hour — the orange flavor deepens and the texture improves significantly.
Add the zest of 1 orange to the butter mixture before creaming for an extra layer of citrus that the liqueur alone won't give you.
Use a roughly chopped 70%+ dark chocolate bar instead of chips — the irregular pieces melt into better pockets.
Roll the balls in a mix of cocoa powder and a pinch of flaky sea salt before baking for a subtle savory contrast.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Dust with a fresh layer of powdered sugar before serving if they've been sitting. Freeze baked cookies for up to 3 months; thaw at room temperature and re-dust before serving.
